P01.note: Three buyer-type sums exceeding thirty years' profit plus 'no wages, rents or repairs' then only share dividends point to a sale; 'no ... rents' kills leased, and the timber merchant makes logged a literal near-fit that the landowner and auctioneer undercut.

P02.note: 'returned the altarpiece as dark with smoke and varnish as it had arrived' kills both scrubbed and uncovered in one phrase; transferred has no support, leaving stabilized from the wax-and-frame sentence.

P03.note: Each distractor has a planted kill: border by 'a wall the city had already outgrown' and quarters on both banks, artery by watchmen keeping barges off, commons by keeping laundry and loiterers off; spring water vs brackish wells plus pipes to fountains gives aqueduct.

P04.note: Relict species 'vanished from every other lake' make it unrepresentative (kills microcosm) and a window on the ice-age past (museum); the yearly layers lure ledger/metronome until 'churned its layers past reading'.

P05.note: 'every benchmark ... sat nine meters lower' (uniform, kills tilted), walls 'still stood' (kills scoured), farms 'planted as before' (kills smothered); anchoring above the village walls nearly hands over submerged, though the island is only partly under water.

P06.note: Scrap silver, bars cast from melted pieces, test nicks and a workshop with furnace and crucibles make it a smith's raw stock; loot and insurance (savings) fit hacksilver hoards generally and must be rejected on the workshop context.

P07.note: 'tiny raised rims, each around a pinhole' alone describes burst blisters; 'brushwork showed ... as clearly as before' kills clouded and 'held tea without a mark' kills cracked; blackened has no support.

P08.note: Road 'below the town, on land the railroad had abandoned' kills fragmented, growth to 26,000 kills drained, city offices and chains kill fossilized; no open field from the city gives engulfed.

P09.note: Every ship cleared customs and took an island pilot through the only channel, so the island controlled entry; warehouses make depot a literal fit, killed by 'that same day ... fully reloaded'; fortress and haven unsupported.

P10.note: Each change 'raised the rate' and bills to lower it 'always failed' kill pendulum and regulator; 'neighboring countries had raised their own ... years before' kills pacemaker, leaving ratchet.

P11.note: One planted phrase per distractor: 'laid as many eggs' kills neutered, 'grew as large ... lived as long' kills milked, the bacterium 'killed both kinds alike' kills immunized; climbing to where ducks feed gives manipulated.

P12.note: Near-freezing chamber, unburned stacked joints, and autumn cuts eaten in late winter combine to cold storage; hearths and children's teeth 'in a camp by the river' kill lodge; the cliff overlooking the ford makes lookout a literal fit.

P13.note: Gutters draining 'whatever the streets carry' into a 'black pond whose smell reaches the market square' hands over cesspool on a surface read; arena and bazaar are off-topic for a fouled flooded pit with nothing to support them, and only bunker gets even a planted kill ('flooded to their roofs').

P14.note: Operators 'formed their own association' and 'Both bodies still bargained there in 1944' give divided and kill doomed/disbanded; the laborers winning a nine-week strike kills defanged.

P15.note: Must combine the floes drifting south with pups nursing two weeks and arriving 'near the shoals where young seals feed' to get raft; seals climbing on to give birth make perch a strong literal fit, and 'almost nothing grows beneath them' kills pantry.

P16.note: Rocky planets 'struck about equally often in both runs' kills umbrella and the belt thinning 'much as it did without the giant' kills slingshot; tether is the near-miss for a swarm held in step, shepherd fits the gathered, co-moving swarm better.

P17.note: Boats and buyers moving four miles to the village makes uprooted the precise reading, but the blank's object is 'the city's fish market', which the rule did choke off, so stifled stays defensible; the fleet growing by a third only argues against stifling the trade, not the city's market.

P18.note: 'every book by some two hundred writers, most of them critics of the occupiers, had gone, along with those writers' catalog cards' hands over purged on its own; 'most shelves stood full and the rare-book room was untouched' kills pulped and plundered.

P19.note: Same festival week, a gate 'carved taller', and city tolls halving point to rivalry; 'no tie to the city temple's' kills offshoot and smaller/wooden kills replica; precursor is not dated out but is weak.

P20.note: 'matched the older company's model part for part, down to the shape of the keys' alone hands over mimicked, reinforced by buying and dismantling it; 'same dealers' makes infiltrated a literal near-fit and outselling lures leapfrogged, but part-for-part copying kills a leap.

P21.note: The draft entering low and leaving high with 'a plume of vapor' over the hill is a chimney in one sentence; the brook 'runs out' kills cistern, bellows is the near-miss (moves air but by pumping), cooler unsupported.

P22.note: 'overran' is ungrammatical after 'had' (needs 'overrun'), so D falls on grammar alone; population halved kills repopulated and 'main street still facing the river landing' kills reoriented.

P23.note: Sand two feet over the lagoon-side reeds and boathouses now two hundred yards from the water give broadened; the keeper driving 'past the lighthouse to the hooked tip' kills cleaved and blunted. The spring sentence about wind lifting the new sand off muddies whether the broadening lasted to the survey.

P24.note: Glass building on the airport highway, weekly tours for ministers and editors, cars lent to officials, dealers pointing buyers to it all add up to showroom; 'never built another plant' kills toehold; schoolhouse and warehouse unsupported.

P25.note: One planted kill each: 'too fast for a barge to tie up' (anchorage), raiders burned its barns (citadel), 'spring floods cover it' (ark); carts reaching the far bank 'by way of the island' gives crossing.

P26.note: The pond-temperature setup lures thermostat, killed by 'leaves as icy in January and as warm in August as the river arrives'; outflow 'a third larger than its inflow' kills sink and makes the lake an added source, and the constant ratio in drought and wet years undercuts valve.

P27.note: Committee 'sat in another country' kills headquarters and reporters handed its address kills embassy; the poet training new arrivals who later edited all the papers gives hothouse, while exiles gathering there makes hub a literal near-fit.

P28.note: Ballads cut from twenty verses to five or six gives stripped; rough voices and tunings kept 'as the engineers had found them' kills smoothed, porches ringing for decades kills silenced, and songs staying in the region kills transplanted.

P29.note: Opened after the last seed merchant closed and turned to cattle once a seed company arrived: a stopgap; 'the district's usual wheat' kills testbed, and being the literal seed source makes wellspring a near-fit that misses the temporariness.

P30.note: Dark mud followed by record harvests in ordinary-rain years gives nourished; winter wheat 'withered as badly as on the dry terraces' kills irrigated (a literal fit for a flood) and water soaking away within weeks kills marooned.

P31.note: Seedlings in 'a dense row along its whole length' give garden; hostel (lodging for travellers) is off-topic for a passage about plants and falls on a surface read; the log spanning the stream makes highway a literal fit, and hatchery is the nursery lure but applies to eggs and animals.

P32.note: 'a single shaft from one deep vein' kills riddled, slopes and cairn looking as in old photographs kill razed and pitted; orange water, vanished trout and dead streamside forest give poisoned.

P33.note: Flow down to a fifth but 'never stopped', narrow enough to step across: pinched; trout moving 'freely up and down it from bend to bend' kills pooled, nearly all alive kills overheated, and the dry white gravel margins make parched a literal near-fit.

P34.note: Stock 'otherwise left untouched' and opened only in failed-harvest years at last year's price is a backstop; ballast is the near-miss (steadying) but implies constant weight rather than use only in failure, while coffer and cudgel are unsupported.

P35.note: Forty pages reduced to one three-minute episode gives distilled; 'still set in the desert capital' kills domesticated, 'kept a single episode' kills fused, and 'in nearly the words of the 1650 text' kills honed.

P36.note: The only keel-deep passage is the gut, with reefs beyond the island, and a boat there collects dues: chokepoint; swells rolling across the crest kill breakwater and 'a few feet covers the rest of the crest' at high water kills causeway; barricade is the near-miss.

P37.note: 'came out of its western end within an hour' kills lair, inn and larder in one phrase; voles burrowing in the bank make larder a literal lure, but east-to-west dispersal through the hedge gives lane.

P38.note: A month each spring of 'trading, racing and weddings' then scattering, quiet the other eleven months, gives fairground; trading makes emporium a literal near-fit but misses racing, weddings and seasonality; a few families growing their own dates undercuts estate.

P39.note: The salt crust lures rinsed, but sown yields stayed half 'as it always had' (kills rinsed and replenished) and stubble left standing kills plowed; upland water plus meadow grasses appearing on the fallow fields must be combined to get reseeded.

P40.note: Larger papers voted to sell and left for a new service while the rest refused: fractured; 'both groups' circulation kept rising' kills dethroned and hamstrung, and the split itself kills homogenized.
